scenes.title: Where and when
narration: Sangini originated in the hilly regions of Nepal as a ritual practice for women of the Brahmin and Chhetri castes.
Its history is tied to the mythological dialogue between Shiva and Parvati, where the dance was established as a form of puja to prevent early widowhood.
It has since spread with the Nepali diaspora into parts of India and Bhutan.

scenes.title: When it is danced
narration: The primary occasions are the festivals of Teej and Tihar.
It serves as a social function for married daughters to reunite with their families and a religious function to seek the blessing of Lord Shiva for the long life of their husbands.
Today it is a living tradition.

scenes.title: Watch it
narration: The dance is performed in a circle, usually in a courtyard or temple setting.
Dancers move with a slow, rhythmic step while balancing objects such as a Kalash (water pot) on their heads or holding a Diyo (oil lamp) on a plate.
The dancers are the sole musicians, singing the accompanying songs as they move.
Watch for Kalash Balancing.

narration: Sangini is traditionally performed without external musical instruments.
The music consists of 'Sangini' songs sung by the dancers themselves.

scenes.title: The costume and the setting
narration: Dancers typically wear traditional Nepali festive attire, often red saris.
The setting is usually the 'Angan' (courtyard) of a house or a temple area, typically in the sylvan surroundings of the Nepali hills.
Key props include copper or brass Kalash vessels and Diyo lamps.

scenes.title: The people
narration: The sources do not name specific historical individuals, as the dance is a communal tradition passed down through the women of the Brahmin and Chhetri communities.
While originating in the Nepali hills, the dance is also practiced by Nepali-speaking communities in India and Bhutan, though specific stylistic differences are not detailed in the sources.
Sangini is categorized as a Nepalese folk and ritual dance, specifically a subclass of the music and dance traditions of the high-caste Nepali groups.
